title: The Easiest Way to Start an Online Business (SaaS)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The speaker uses an affiliate link for HighLevel and says he receives a kickback (lines 90–93).

stated_problem.quote: because I don't even know how to code and you probably don't either
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: White-label SaaS on HighLevel
idea.one_liner: Choose a business niche, brand HighLevel's software, and sell it to that niche for recurring subscription revenue.
idea.customer: Businesses in a selected niche, such as dental practices, real estate agents, fitness coaches, e-commerce brands, or coaches.
idea.offer: Branded software delivered through HighLevel, with onboarding, setup calls, and training.

key_quotes.quote: choose the white label account use an AI generated logo pick some colors and boom you've got software
the welcome emails the setup calls and the training materials get this right you can use AI to generate it
you're going to have to learn sales you're going to have to learn marketing you're going to have to deal with difficult clients
pick one company from this awards list spend a week learning everything you can about them and then start putting out feelers

claims.claim: The speaker says 67 businesses make between 50,000 and 500,000 per month by white-labeling the same $300 software.
claims.quote: guys I'm no conspiracy theorist but I just found 67 businesses making between 50,000 and 500,000 per month and they're all white labeling the same $300 software

claims.claim: One company reportedly grew from zero to 1.8 million in 11 months.
claims.quote: one of these companies went from 0 to 1.8 million in 11 months

claims.claim: Another company reportedly charges $500 per month for a service that costs almost nothing to deliver.
claims.quote: another one is charging $500 per month for something that cost them almost nothing to deliver

claims.claim: HighLevel award tiers require 100, 500, or 1,000 SaaS customer subaccounts.
claims.quote: to win a diamond gold or platinum award using High Level you have to have either 100 500 or 1,000 sub accounts aka SAS customers

claims.claim: The speaker says white-label services sell for $100 to $2,000 per month.
claims.quote: these are $100 to $2,000 a month services that are all delivered with someone else's software someone else's code

claims.claim: Some companies reportedly charge a minimum of $100 per month, while others charge $3,000 or $4,000 per month.
claims.quote: most of these companies are charging at a bare minimum $100 a month some of them charging three or $4,000 a month

claims.claim: The speaker estimates award winners may have 1,000 to 10,000 customers.
claims.quote: the diamond award winners have at least a,000 customers might have 10,000 for all we know

claims.claim: At an assumed 1,000 customers paying $100 per month, revenue would be $100,000 per month.
claims.quote: let's say they have a,000 exactly and they charge the bare minimum $100 a month that's $100,000 a month

claims.claim: The speaker says HighLevel costs 97 per month.
claims.quote: they slapped their logo on it and we're talking High Lee cost 97 bucks a month

claims.claim: HighLevel's white-label service with AI features costs $300 per month.
claims.quote: there's a free trial it's 300 a month if you want to use their white labeling service with some AI features

claims.claim: Unlimited white-label subaccounts cost $500 per month, and the speaker says to wait until customer revenue reaches at least $500 per month before committing.
claims.quote: it's $500 a month but you don't have to commit to that until you have enough customers that are paying you at least $500 a month

claims.claim: The speaker says his affiliate link offers a 30-day trial instead of the usual 14-day trial.
claims.quote: you get a 30-day free trial of High Level instead of a 14-day free trial anywhere else will offer you 14 days

claims.claim: The speaker says the branded software can look like it costs thousands of dollars per month.
claims.quote: pick some colors and boom you've got software that looks like it costs thousands of dollars a month

acquisition_channels.details: He recommends researching and copying proven ad angles, offers, pricing, and website structure.
He recommends talking to potential customers and getting them on the phone.

ideas.delivery: The founder brands a HighLevel account, then provides software access and handles onboarding emails, setup calls, training, sales, and client support.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK prospecting, cold calls must screen TPS/CTPS; cold email should be limited to companies with an opt-out. UK GDPR applies to customer data and its processing.

idea.name: Agent CRM
idea.one_liner: A CRM positioned specifically for insurance agents, sold as a monthly subscription.
idea.offer: Customer relationship management software framed for insurance agents.

key_quotes.quote: agent CRM insurance agent CRM that's customer relationship management software let's see what they charge $97 a month
marketing software built especially for insurance agent and financial planners only $47 per month
they're still offering a 14-day free trial which means that that is part of their killer offer
they are getting 12 to 16,000 visitors per week

claims.claim: The speaker reports a $97 monthly price and over a,000 customers.
claims.quote: let's see what they charge $97 a month and they have over a,000 customers

claims.claim: An earlier website listed a $47 monthly price.
claims.quote: marketing software built especially for insurance agent and financial planners only $47 per month

claims.claim: The speaker says the company later doubled its pricing.
claims.quote: they've since doubled their pricing and they've simplified their language in their headline which is critical

claims.claim: The company offers a 14-day free trial.
claims.quote: they're still offering a 14-day free trial which means that that is part of their killer offer

claims.claim: The speaker reports 12,000 to 16,000 weekly visitors.
claims.quote: they are getting 12 to 16,000 visitors per week

claims.claim: The speaker estimates 15,000 weekly visitors would mean 60,000 monthly visitors and 1,800 free trials at a 3% rate.
claims.quote: let's say very conservatively okay 15,000 visitors per week equals 60,000 per month you take 3% of that and you've got 1,800 free trials per month

claims.claim: At a hypothetical 20% conversion rate, 1,800 trials would yield 360 paid customers per month.
claims.quote: 1,800 trials a month let's say only only 20% of them convert to paid that's 360 new paid customers every month

claims.claim: The speaker estimates that 360 new customers paying $100 would mean $36,000 monthly recurring revenue.
claims.quote: times 100 is $36,000 of MR monthly recurring revenue every month could be more could be less I don't know

claims.claim: The speaker reports that 82% of traffic is from the United States and 72% is direct.
claims.quote: 82% of their traffic is coming from the United States 72% of it is direct which is the highest intent of traffic

claims.claim: The speaker reports 1 and a.5% paid traffic and 19% organic traffic.
claims.quote: 1 and a.5% is paid which means they're probably not running very many paid ads 19% organic which is encouraging

claims.claim: The speaker reports 6% referral traffic.
claims.quote: 6% at referral traffic so this tells me that whoever owns this business is doing a ton of outbound call text email

acquisition_channels.details: The speaker infers outbound calls from the traffic sources; he does not verify this with the business.
The speaker infers outbound texts to prospects from the traffic sources; he does not verify this with the business.
The speaker infers outbound email from the traffic sources; he does not verify this with the business.
The speaker also mentions voice agents and ringless voicemail drops as inferred outbound methods.

ideas.delivery: Customers use the CRM software online; the speaker describes it as HighLevel white-label software.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The speaker infers outbound marketing texts to insurance-agent prospects. Unsolicited marketing texts to UK individuals or sole traders are prohibited without consent or a valid soft opt-in.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Cold calls must screen TPS/CTPS; cold email should be limited to limited companies with an opt-out. UK GDPR applies to prospect and customer data.
